title: Delegation Verify Scorecard
desc: ROOT's rubric at the mandatory phase-B verify gate between a delegate's prototype+self-test and the ROOT/Opus wiring. Score each criterion against the agent's ACTUAL diff + self-test transcript, never its report. Any FAIL = send back + record the failure reflex. Built from 2026-07-13 lessons (Haiku code-drop, codex silent no-op).
steps: HOW TO USE: apply this at phase B -- the NON-SKIPPABLE verify gate between a delegate's prototype+self-test and the ROOT/Opus wiring (see agent-dispatch-preflight delegation-lifecycle). Score each item below PASS/FAIL against the agent's ACTUAL git diff + its self-test transcript, NOT its summary. ALL pass -> proceed to wiring. ANY fail -> send the specific gap back to the agent (still prototype phase) AND record a failure reflex (attribution: delegate's own error -> its model reflection; bad/ambiguous brief -> ROOT's reflection).

1. SPEC-COMPLETENESS: check off EVERY required piece of the brief against the diff, one by one. A silently DROPPED part (a guard/branch/option the brief specified) = FAIL. This is the number-1 catch -- the signature cheap-tier failure is dropping one piece of a multi-part spec (2026-07-13: Haiku shipped swap plus PIN guard but dropped the skill-kind guard).

2. NEGATIVE-PATH TESTED: the agent must self-test the REFUSE / error / edge / bounds paths, not just the happy path. A guard is only proven when shown actually REFUSING the thing it guards. Happy-path-only self-test = FAIL (an untested guard is presumed absent).

3. CLAIM = REALITY: help text, code comments, and the agent's report must match what the code ACTUALLY enforces. Any text asserting a behavior the code does not implement = FAIL (2026-07-13: help said merit-ranked only while nothing enforced it).

4. GROUND-TRUTH VERIFIED: ROOT confirms via git diff plus a LIVE run of the freshly-built artifact -- never the agent's it-works or a bare exit 0 (codex can exit 0 with zero changes; Haiku confabulates all-tests-pass). Static/report evidence = FAIL until run.
5. STAYED-IN-LANE: prototype plus self-test ONLY -- NO live deploy, NO git commit (wiring is post-gate ROOT/Opus). A cheap agent that already deployed/committed = FAIL: revert and re-gate.
6. NO-BANDAID plus CORRECT: reuses existing functions (no duplicated logic), correct bounds, fail-open where appropriate, builds with 0 errors (or the exact errors are reported).

7. VERDICT plus ATTRIBUTION: all PASS -> WIRE it (ROOT/Opus, atomic cutover plus immediate fast health-check). Any FAIL -> (a) return the specific gap to the agent to fix, (b) record the reflex in the correct reflection per the attribution rule. NOTE: these criteria are MERIT-ranked -- reorder them with --like/--dislike as real cases teach which catches matter most (this scorecard is itself a living reflex).

ATTRIBUTION GATE -- on any FAIL, check ROOT's OWN brief BEFORE blaming the delegate (user 2026-07-13). SCOPE: this scorecard scores only the delegate's CONTROLLABLE output -- NEVER harness/infra bugs (cross-family skill-read credit, the session-transcript resolver, gate flakiness are NOT the delegate's fault; do NOT score them). Those harness bugs belong in the REFLECTION skill instead -- that is where a capable ROOT, reading its reflection before it delegates, SEES the known bug and fixes it. When a scorecard criterion FAILs, FIRST ask: was the BRIEF contract-complete plus unambiguous -- clear spec, right files named, exit criterion, and the dropped/failed piece EXPLICITLY stated? If the brief was ambiguous / under-scoped / never named the missing piece, the FAIL is ROOT's BAD-INSTRUCTION: the reflex goes to ROOT's reflection (opus-self-reflection), NOT the delegate's, and ROOT RE-BRIEFS (does not re-blame). Only if the brief WAS contract-complete and the delegate still dropped a named piece / confabulated is it the delegate's fault -> its model reflection. So YES, bad instruction IS scored -- as ROOT's, caught by this gate -- so the cheap tier is never scapegoated for the orchestrator's briefing failure. Runs before criterion 7's verdict. Cross: claude-code-agent-tier-routing step 16 (failure attribution); opus-self-reflection.

Only 2 of ~18 attempts (both early in the session, low total transcript size) succeeded. Per this scorecard's own ATTRIBUTION GATE (step 9): this is harness/infra gate-flakiness, NOT delegate-controllable output -- scored nowhere on a delegate, recorded here as the reflection artifact ROOT should read before its next delegation cycle. Suggest filed with repro steps. WORKAROUND: keep dispatching small genuinely-useful real tasks and retrying opportunistically; it does eventually clear, just unreliably. INCIDENT: ROOT's own exit criterion escapes this scorecard, because it looks like the ruler rather than the thing measured -- and two OPPOSITE wrong answers passed it unchallenged. WHEN: at phase B, before scoring any item below, whenever the brief's pass condition is a threshold or inequality (greater than zero, at least one, non-empty) and the correct answer was knowable in advance. HOW: rewrite the criterion as an EXACT VALUE against a NAMED ground truth before accepting the result -- not 'call sites greater than zero' but 'exactly 2 call lines, in exactly 1 file, and that file is <name>' -- then ask the one-question diagnostic, what OTHER value would ALSO have passed this, and if the answer is 'almost any' the green is noise; for the surrounding discipline run wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring-ref and wkappbot skill search exit criterion ground truth. WHY: measured 2026-08-27 on one delegation twice in a row -- the brief ROOT wrote required call sites greater than zero for a known-wired file; the first return was 0 and the second was 33, while the truth was 2 lines in 1 file and the agent itself blamed worktree copies for the inflation, so a threshold that cannot separate 2 from 33 cannot separate 0 from 1 either. This rubric scores the delegate's diff and transcript because those are visibly someone else's claims, while the pass criterion was authored by the same person doing the scoring and is therefore never put on trial -- an exact assertion that breaks on a legitimate repo change is a FEATURE, forcing a deliberate update instead of silently widening to admit anything.

VERIFIED: item zero has a POSITIVE instance -- a criterion I wrote was refuted BEFORE it shipped, and what caught it was testing the PAYLOAD against live state rather than the mechanism, which no fixture-fed self-test can do. WHEN: you are about to dispatch a brief whose core is a RULE you invented (a threshold, a predicate, an attribution test), and especially when the self-test cases you specified would all pass by construction. HOW: before the dispatch lands, evaluate your own rule BY HAND against live state and check its answer against ground truth you can independently name, then read wkappbot skill read wkareyouready for the worked example and wkappbot skill read foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore for the proxy-substitution failure it belongs to. WHY: fixing the wkareyouready -Start residue refusal I specified that a dirty file is YOURS when its LastWriteTime is at or after this session's transcript CreationTime -- a complete brief, five-part SPEC, seven named cases, the git-stderr and repo-root traps quoted from the consumer's own comments, and every case would have passed. Run against the real tree it refuted me in one command: session start 01:19:16, four dirty files at or after it, exactly TWO mine (both mirrors of one skill edit I had just made) while sonnet-reflection at 01:29:12 and claude-session-handoff-ref at 01:26:17 were written by PEER SESSIONS on this shared desktop inside my own window. The rule over-counted by two, and the two it invented were files I am forbidden to revert, so it reproduced the exact unsatisfiable refusal it existed to remove, only smaller. Mtime is a PROXY for authorship; the transcript IS authorship, so the amended rule reads the session's own JSONL for Edit/Write file_paths and wkappbot skill edit ids and demotes mtime to a corroborator. The part that belongs in a verify rubric: injected fixtures prove the mechanism counts what it is HANDED, never that it is handed the right thing, so a 9/9 green suite can sit on a rule that is wrong about reality and phase B, which scores the transcript, would have passed it. A criterion you cannot hand-check against something you already know is a criterion shipped on faith.
